params.test: POST-HOC: pooled single-segment site-bootstrap null for A_concatenated
params.metric: hamming p-distance fed directly to Rips (NO embedding)
params.reason: the pre-stated site bootstrap of the concatenated alignment cannot be a null for reassortment: resampling columns leaves each genome's row, and therefore its segment combination, intact

runs.preprocessing: sites resampled with replacement WITHIN each single segment; the resulting A and B values pooled across all eight segments

stats.name: A_max_h1_persistence_concat
stats.null_model: pooled single-segment site bootstrap (clonal, non-reassorting data at this sample size)
stats.multiplicity: post hoc; not pre-registered and not corrected

controls.description: this null is drawn from CLONAL data (single segments are trees), so it is the distribution of A when no reassortment has occurred -- unlike the pre-stated site bootstrap of the concatenation, which preserves reassortment

DISCLOSED LIMITATION: the null's alignments are shorter (865-2369 columns) than the concatenation (14008), so this null differs from the observed statistic in length as well as in reassortment. No long non-reassorting alignment of these organisms exists to draw from.

findings.claim: POST-HOC, with a null that can actually be one: A_concatenated = 0.04199 against a pooled single-segment site-bootstrap null of 200 draws (median 0.00559, max 0.02128) gives p = 0.00498. With criteria (ii) and (iii) already met, the published contrast of Chan, Carlsson & Rabadan (2013) is reproduced on this criterion set: PASS.
findings.caveat: POST HOC: this null was chosen after the pre-stated one turned out to be ill-posed. The pre-stated run and its FAIL verdict remain in the database unchanged. The null's alignments are shorter than the concatenation, which is a stated confound.
findings.reference: Chan, Carlsson & Rabadan, PNAS 110:18566 (2013); the same null the 2026-09-19 genetics validation used (its p_A was 0.0025 over 400 draws)
